$comment: spreadsheets.values.update -> PUT v4/spreadsheets/{spreadsheetId}/values/{range}, request+response ValueRange/UpdateValuesResponse. Read from Google's own discovery document 2026-10-01. Unlike row_append (values.append, which finds the next empty row below a range and never touches existing cells), update OVERWRITES exactly the cells inside the given range -- said plainly, since the two actions sound alike and do different things to data already there.
title: Write Google Sheets values
description: Overwrite the cell values of a range. Existing values in that range are replaced, not pushed down.
$sideEffectsComment: Re-sending the same values to the same range leaves the sheet in the same state both times -- unlike row_append, nothing is pushed down or duplicated by a retry.

config.label: Range
config.description: In A1 notation. The values written fill this range from its top-left cell -- more rows or columns than the range covers are written anyway, following Google's own documented behavior; fewer leave the rest of the range untouched.

config.label: Row values
config.description: The cells to write, comma separated, left to right, one row. For more than one row, call this action once per row.

config.label: How to interpret the values
config.description: USER_ENTERED parses the cells the way typing them would -- so =SUM(A1:A2) becomes a formula. RAW stores exactly the characters given.

options.label: As if typed (formulas and dates parsed)
